solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Being noisy is possibly vice of ours

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the adjective, as in 'being vociferous'

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the following words may be reordered

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that our particular failing is making too much noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Vociferous describes someone loudly and insistently expressing their views, so it fits a person making a lot of noise.

clue.text: Very grown-up to avoid opening of dark cellar

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep away from it, so that letter is dropped from the word
the opening of a word is its very start, so only its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: An adult hoping to dodge a gloomy basement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening of dark' names the letter to be removed from the grown-up word, not a letter to add.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault is an underground chamber, such as a wine store beneath a building, so it can be a cellar.

clue.text: I obsess over timepiece, timepiece found in opening of college cupboard

definitions.note: a first-person description that the person named by the answer might give of themselves

indicators.note: the opening of a word is where it starts, so just its first letter is used
found in says one item sits inside another, so a word is placed within the cupboard word

parts.note: a locker is a small lockable cupboard
a watch is a timepiece worn on the wrist

explanation.surface: Someone admits fussing over their watch, kept in a cupboard at college.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'timepiece' goes inside LOCKER, which follows the C of college; the first is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock-watcher is an employee who keeps checking the time, eager for the working day to end.

clue.text: Market offering equal opportunities?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gathering for trade, as in a trade or craft event
second meaning: just and even-handed to everyone

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an employer's market or fair-trade promise; the noun and the adjective are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair is a periodic market or show, and fair also means just and impartial, treating everyone equally.

clue.text: Organised party with Mike on an irregular basis

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for the adjective, as in 'at random'

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone hosts the odd party with a friend called Mike, not on any schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' looks like an anagram signal but simply gives RAN, as in ran the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means happening without a pattern or method, which is the sense of something done irregularly.

clue.text: Unusual rum label covering a lot of things

definitions.note: a participle phrase for the adjectival use, as in 'umbrella term'

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary order, so the letters that follow come out rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd label on a bottle of rum that covers many products.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbrella organisation or term is one that groups many different things together under a single heading.

clue.text: Criminal activity? Son with mother's handbag possibly about right

definitions.note: the question mark marks a definition by example

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the single letter
possibly hints that the bag word may appear in another arrangement

parts.note: ma is mother, with the possessive S
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A son snatching his mother's handbag might be a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The handbag is both part of the surface theft and the letters to be rearranged; 'about' wraps those letters around the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash-and-grab is a robbery where a thief breaks a window and seizes goods, a type of crime.

clue.text: Equipment to look after tailless pet

indicators.note: without a tail means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to tend is to look after

explanation.surface: Gear needed for caring for a pet with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitten is a young cat, commonly kept as a household pet.

clue.text: I put on a different description of ideal world

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective that describes an ideal world

indicators.note: different signals the letters are put into another order

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone writes a fresh account of a perfect society.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian is the adjective for Utopia, Thomas More's imagined perfect society, so it describes an ideal world.

clue.text: Disney character in book with reduced scope

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure appears in a book with limited range.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is the young deer who is the title character of the 1942 Disney animated film.

clue.text: Steal post, disposing of first letter

indicators.note: getting rid of the first letter means the word is cut at its start

parts.note: a stake is a post driven into the ground

explanation.surface: An instruction to steal mail after throwing away the opening letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like mail, which the first letter suggests, but it is a wooden pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something that is not yours is to steal it; take is a common synonym.

clue.text: Particular group bridging river in Southwestern county

indicators.note: a bridge spans something, so the two words reach across and enclose the single letter

parts.note: some can mean a particular, unspecified one
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A certain club building a bridge over a river in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: SOME and SET go either side of R. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is a county in the south-west of England, home to Bath and Taunton.

clue.text: Native American mostly adopting expert methodology

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the shortened word takes another inside it
mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the Apache are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Native American taking on a specialist's working methods.
explanation.walkthrough: The expert goes in after the first two letters of the shortened tribe name, not at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An approach is a way of tackling a problem, which is what a methodology is.

clue.text: Force and pressure producing pain in muscle?

definitions.note: the question mark marks a definition by example

parts.note: to cram is to force or stuff in
P is the abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: Strain and stress bringing on a pain in a muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp is a sudden painful involuntary contraction of a muscle.

clue.text: Birmingham maybe securing a victory, initially hollow

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the city word holds the others inside

parts.note: Birmingham is an example of a city

indicators.note: initially points to the start of a word, so only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A Birmingham team clinching a win, at first looking empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birmingham' suggests a football club, but it is just an example of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity is an empty space within something, which is a hollow.

clue.text: Study not productive involving reading primarily

indicators.note: involving means including, so the single letter goes inside the word
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Studying gets nowhere if it mostly involves reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn is to acquire knowledge by studying, so the verbs are close synonyms.

clue.text: Shocked a leader in Guardian has to appear before leader in Times

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its front letter, so only that is used; this applies to both newspaper names

explanation.surface: Someone appalled that a Guardian editorial runs ahead of the Times leader.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'leader' is also a newspaper editorial, which the surface plays on; here it is just a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or shock, so it is a synonym of shocked.

clue.text: A lot of sin and passion seen around a religious dwelling

indicators.note: seen around means placed on either side, so the two words enclose the single letter
a lot of means most but not all, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Plenty of wickedness and lust found around a churchman's home.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the sinful surface for a clergyman's home; the shortened sin and the passion sit on either side of the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for a vicar, a Church of England parish priest.

clue.text: Plan One not working? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means just short of complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a dead machine is not working

explanation.surface: A scheme that fails to work, or almost fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not working' tempts toward IDLE; it is DEAD, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a plan or intention, as in 'the idea is to leave early'.

clue.text: Additional building has former Queen cross

explanation.surface: An extension where a past monarch is annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry but is the letter shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: An annex is an extra building attached to or near a main one, providing more space.

clue.text: One auction disposing of a piece of land

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: disposing of something means getting rid of it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: the letter taken out of the auction word

explanation.surface: A single auction selling off a plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Greek character and article coming with thanks

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A Greek person and a newspaper piece arrive with gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, and character here means letter.

clue.text: Orchestra and artist interrupting an unimpressive performer

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so these go inside the following words

parts.note: taken as written; split around the inserted letters
LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An orchestra and painter breaking in on a lacklustre performer.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a horse that does not finish in the places, so by extension anyone who fails to impress.

clue.text: Countess's foremost milliner linked to TV gossip

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's chief hatmaker connected to television tittle-tattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gossip' looks like chatter about TV, but it names a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterbox is someone who talks incessantly, and a gossip is a person who chatters about others.
